fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: The review planning notes highlight that this paper provides methodological context for intracellular metabolism, explaining that nucleotides are primarily intracellular while extracellular purines exist as parent forms due to phosphatase activity. It supports the biological rationale for using PBMCs over RBCs for immune-related metabolic profiling due to de novo synthesis capabilities in nucleated cells. The planning also flags the DBS hydrolysis finding as a cautionary example for sample handling in clinical trials.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this study to benchmark technical validation parameters (precision, accuracy, stability) for metabolite quantification methods in the review. Cite the PBMC vs. RBC concentration differences when discussing immune cell metabolic baselines. Continue searching for specific consensus guidelines or validated protocols for serum and tumor tissue samples, and for SCFA measurement methods, as these remain open gaps.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The specific success criteria for standardized measurement in human tumor microenvironment or serum remain unaddressed, as this study focused on blood cell lysates. There is no evidence of a consensus guideline or widely adopted standard for serum/tumor metabolite quantification in this text. Additionally, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are not covered, only purine nucleotides. The study represents a single-laboratory validation rather than a field-wide consensus.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: This study developed and validated an LC-MS/MS method for quantifying adenosine, guanosine, and inosine nucleotides (mono- and triphosphate forms) in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), red blood cells (RBCs), and dried blood spots (DBS). The authors reported absolute quantification ranges (e.g., inosine triphosphate 0.25–50 pmol/sample) with interassay precision ≤15% and accuracy within −11.5% to 14.7%. Key findings include significantly higher nucleotide concentrations in PBMCs compared to RBCs (5.6-fold for ITP) and instability of triphosphates in DBS samples (26% lower TP levels due to hydrolysis). The method requires solid-phase extraction and dephosphorylation steps to measure molar equivalent nucleosides, with strict controls for environmental contamination affecting low-abundance analytes like ITP.
